Unlocking and issuance deserve separate columns. An already-issued allocation can become transferable without increasing total supply. A transfer condition, a provider classification and a market transaction are different observations.

A comparable total-supply reconciliation starts with opening supply, adds confirmed issuance, subtracts confirmed burns and includes documented methodology adjustments. An ordinary transfer is not issuance, and a payment from a treasury is not automatically a burn.

Several news pages repeating one announcement do not provide several independent proofs. If only one person knows how to perform a reconciliation, it is not a process — it is a risk that materialises the day that person is unavailable.

When only one person knows how to reconcile a particular balance — which spreadsheet to use, which adjustments to make, which exceptions are “normal” — the organisation has a risk, not a process. If that person is unavailable during the close, the reconciliation either does not happen or is performed by someone guessing at the method.
Every reconciliation should be documented well enough that a competent finance professional who has never performed it before can follow the steps and reach the same result.
